Calibration counts groups, not items. A group is the same flagged line for the same function and rule across worker states and attempts, so correlated items count once. Label until the held-out side has at least 29 independent negative groups and at least 10 positive groups.
With 0 held-out false accepts, 29 negative groups give a one-sided 95% upper bound of 0.0981, under the 0.10 cap.
One group takes about 1 to 2 minutes in

The selection side also needs labelled groups to choose thresholds. Labelling about 100 groups in total takes roughly 2 to 3 hours.

Three calibration commands copy text from the harness history into files, and they scrub that text before they write.
scrub the values of environment variables with secret-looking names. They also scrub
The scrub also finds each secret of 8 or more characters in URL-encoded or base64 form, in JSON keys, values, and scalars.
If a secret shorter than 8 characters occurs in the history, the command refuses to write, because the scrub cannot replace it safely.
The scrub misses multi-step and non-standard encodings, so review the output of all three commands before you commit it.

Every confirmed-good checkpoint of a settled epoch feeds the librarian, whatever the adjudication mode. The feed is on by default, but production runs do not consume it.

Each attempt that starts a kernel run records that run before the model call, so a replay cites the run whose output it returns. If that write fails, the kernel ends the run without a model call and the job retries.
